questions.question: On a new Brazil instance, an analyst wants to build a bar chart of open incidents by assignment group in the Visualization Designer and keep it in the library for reuse. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Create a Core UI report and place it on a dashboard
Create a visualization from the Data Visualizations library
Open the Indicators library and create an automated indicator
Open the Migration Center and migrate an existing report

explanation.correct: On net new Brazil instances, Reporting is replaced by Data Visualizations. The analyst navigates to All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations, selects Create data visualization, and picks the visualization type (here a bar). Users with the itil, report_user, admin, or viz_creator role can build visualizations in the Visualization Designer, and anything created there is saved to the Library, so it can be reused. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/create-dv-donut-ac.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: On net new Brazil instances Core UI Reporting is replaced by Data Visualizations, and Core UI reports cannot be placed on a Platform Analytics dashboard.
The Indicators library creates KPIs (automated, formula, manual, or external) that act as data sources. Creating one does not build a chart in the Visualization Designer.
The Migration Center moves existing Core UI dashboards, reports, filters, and widgets into Platform Analytics. It does not create a new chart from scratch.

source.excerpt: If you need custom charts, go to All, Platform Analytics, Library, Data Visualizations, or use the Column Context menus and lists to create charts directly from the data.

questions.question: An analyst wants a new visualization that reuses most settings of an existing library visualization, without changing the original that several dashboards already display. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Edit the original visualization and save it to the library
Duplicate the existing visualization and edit the copy
Certify the existing visualization and then edit it
Add the existing visualization to another dashboard

explanation.correct: Duplicating a visualization (More actions menu > Duplicate in the Visualization Designer) lets you use aspects of the source in a copy. The copy gets a new name with the suffix - Copy, keeps every other setting, and is saved automatically. The analyst can then change the copy freely, while the original and the dashboards that show it stay untouched. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/duplicate-dv-ac.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Saving edits to a library visualization affects every dashboard that shows it, which is exactly what the analyst wants to avoid here.
Certifying only marks a visualization as company-approved for reuse. It does not create a separate copy, so later edits would still change the original.
Adding the visualization to another dashboard places the same library visualization there. It does not produce an independent copy that can be edited separately.

source.excerpt: It's often easier to build charts starting from a filtered list or existing visualization, where configuration options are pre-provided. It's best practice to duplicate an existing visualization, and then edit your copy to fit your needs.

questions.question: When configuring a data visualization, a user can choose either a Table or an Indicator data source. What is the key difference between the two?

options.text: Table sources need admin rights; indicators suit any viewer
Tables hold current data; indicators track values over time
Table sources need a subscription; indicators come in the base system
Table sources draw charts; indicators display a single score

explanation.correct: A Table data source is the set of records that make up the current state of your data. An Indicator (KPI) records changes to table data over a period of time and is used to find trends and forecast. The docs put it simply: tables contain current data, and to see trends over time you need an indicator, which is calculated from table values collected over time. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/indicator-vs-table-data-source-selection.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Table sources do not require admin rights. Any user with access to the data can create a data visualization from it, and table data is governed by access controls.
Both Table and Indicator data sources are available in the base system. Separate subscriptions apply to sources such as MetricBase or Health Log Analytics.
Indicator data sources work with many visualization types, such as pie and donut charts and time series, not only single scores.

source.excerpt: One-time reporting shows, where are we today? While performance analytics reveals trends over time.

questions.question: A service owner wants a visualization that shows where this month's average resolution time sits between a minimum and a maximum expected value. Which two data visualization types are designed for this? (Choose two)

options.text: Dial visualization
Pareto bar visualization
Gauge visualization
Heatmap visualization

explanation.correct: Score visualizations show a single value. Dial visualizations show where a single value lies across a range from minimum to maximum expected values. Gauges do the same and also let you set colored data ranges that help users understand what the value means. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/data-visualization-type-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pareto bar visualizations help you identify the most important dimension in a large set of dimensions. They show columns in descending order with a cumulative-percentage line, not a single value within a range.
Heatmaps show the relationship between two table fields or indicator breakdowns through changes in color. They do not place a single value between a minimum and a maximum.

source.excerpt: Other visualization types include speedometer, dial, single score, pie, semi-donut, bubble, and text analytics.

questions.question: A team lead without the ui_builder_admin role wants a Platform Analytics dashboard of data visualizations and filters that colleagues can later duplicate and export. Which kind of dashboard fits?

options.text: A technical dashboard built in UI Builder
A dashboard created with the inline editor
A Core UI responsive dashboard with widgets
A Usage Insights dashboard for the team

explanation.correct: Platform Analytics distinguishes dashboards created inline from technical dashboards. An inline dashboard can be created with any role and holds data visualizations, filters, headings, images, simple lists, and rich text. It can be duplicated and exported. A technical dashboard needs the ui_builder_admin role and cannot be duplicated or exported, so the inline editor fits this team lead. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/technical-vs-in-line-dashboards.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Technical dashboards can only be created with the ui_builder_admin role, and they cannot be duplicated or exported, so this option fails the requirements.
Core UI responsive dashboards show Core UI reports and widgets and are in maintenance mode. They are not Platform Analytics dashboards of data visualizations.
Usage Insights provides dashboard views for monitoring how users engage with applications. It is not a dashboard type for building your own analytics.

source.excerpt: Dashboards can be responsive or non-responsive. Non-responsive dashboards have limits on who can create, view, and edit them.

questions.question: In the Visualization Designer, a user is building a pie chart of incidents and wants it to count only open incidents using the predefined Incidents.Open condition. Where is this configured?

options.text: In the Header and border section
In the data source filters
In the Presentation section
In the Data update section

explanation.correct: Which records a visualization includes is set on its data source. When you choose a Table source, you can filter it by custom or predefined conditions, and configured report sources appear in the Predefined conditions list. The docs bubble visualization example picks the Incident [incident] table and adds the predefined condition Incidents.Open in the Filters section, so the visualization only shows active incidents. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/create-dv-donut-ac.html and https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/dv-example-bubble.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Header and border covers the title, description, border, and header options such as refresh and export. None of these settings changes which records are counted.
Presentation controls display and color settings such as the legend, data labels, and color type. It does not filter the underlying records.
Data update holds options like Follow filters, which makes the visualization respond to interactive dashboard filters. It is not a fixed condition on the source.

source.excerpt: Data, choose where your data comes from, either a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table.

questions.question: A user has just saved a new data visualization in the Visualization Designer and wants it on the Incidents Overview dashboard, which they can edit. What should they do?

options.text: Export the visualization and upload it to the dashboard
Recreate the chart as a Core UI report on the dashboard
Use Add to Dashboard > Add to existing dashboard
Certify the visualization so dashboards pick it up

explanation.correct: After saving, the user expands Add to Dashboard and chooses Add to existing dashboard. They pick Incidents Overview in the Select dashboard field and select Add to dashboard. The dashboard opens in the inline editor with the visualization as its last element. The user needs access to the data, ownership of the visualization or a share of it, and the right to edit the dashboard. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/add-dv-new-db.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Visualizations reach a dashboard through Add to Dashboard or the dashboard's Add new element menu. Exporting and uploading is not how elements are added.
Core UI reports cannot be placed on a Platform Analytics dashboard. Data visualizations must be added there instead.
Certification only marks a visualization as company-approved for reuse. It does not place the visualization on any dashboard.

source.excerpt: To add a visualization to a dashboard, either create a dashboard first and add the visualization as an element, or save the visualization and select Add to Dashboard for a new or existing dashboard.

questions.question: An analyst looks at last month's score for an automated indicator that has Collect records selected and wants to see which incidents made up that score. What does Performance Analytics store that makes this possible?

options.text: Indicator scores entered manually each month
Snapshots of the records behind each score
Breakdowns defined on the indicator
Scheduled exports of the indicator's dashboard

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics data collection jobs collect scores and snapshots. A snapshot is the list of records (sys_ids) collected at the same time as the scores for those records, so you can see which records made up a score. Snapshots are made only for automated indicators with Collect records selected. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/c_ClctData.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: You can set indicator scores manually, and the docs suggest this for indicators measured once a month, quarter, or year. Snapshots, the lists of records behind scores, are made only for automated indicators with Collect records selected.
In a visualization, you can filter indicator scores by breakdowns and elements. The lists of records (sys_ids) collected at the time a score is collected are snapshots, not breakdowns.
A scheduled export automates the export and mailing of dashboards and data visualizations. It does not store the records behind an indicator score.

source.excerpt: PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions.

questions.question: A manager wants a visualization showing how the number of open incidents changes over time, with the emphasis on the overall trend. Which visualization type do the docs suggest as the default choice?

options.text: Pie visualization
Line visualization
Dial visualization
Pivot table visualization

explanation.correct: When you create a data visualization, you select the type that suits the data. Time series types show data over time, and the line type connects data points with straight lines to emphasize the trend. The docs call line visualizations the default choice for a time series and recommend a line when you are unsure. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/data-visualization-type-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pie visualizations compare parts of a whole whose segments total 100%. They do not show how a value changes over time.
A dial shows where a single value lies between a minimum and a maximum. It does not show change over time.
A pivot table is a multidimensional view that aggregates fields across rows and columns. It is not the suggested way to show a trend over time.

source.excerpt: Type, pick from over 20 chart types for your visualization.

questions.question: A user's bar visualization is finished, but they want the legend shown below the chart and a different color scheme. Which configuration section of the Visualization Designer should they use?

options.text: Header and border
Data source
Presentation
Chart interaction

explanation.correct: Under Presentation you set display and color information for the visualization. This includes Show legend and Legend position (Above, Below, Right, or Left), data labels, and Colors with a color type setting. Moving the legend below the chart and changing the color scheme both happen here. The chart title is set in Header and border instead. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/create-dv-bar-ac.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Header and border covers the chart title, description, border, and header options. Legend placement and color type are not set there.
The data source decides which table or indicator data the chart shows and how it is filtered. It does not control the legend or colors.
Chart interaction controls what happens when viewers select a data point, such as drilling down. It does not change the legend or colors.

source.excerpt: Presentation, customize the appearance, including color, titles, and legend adjustments.

questions.question: A manager wants the scores of an automated resolved-incidents indicator collected every day from now on, without anyone entering data. What should the administrator set up?

options.text: A scheduled data collection job
Monthly manual entry of indicator scores
A one-time historical data collection job
An import of scores from a spreadsheet

explanation.correct: For ongoing collection, the docs say that if you need to measure indicators more often than monthly, or want to eliminate any human involvement, you should use a scheduled data collection job. A scheduled job regularly collects indicator scores and snapshots. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/c_ClctData.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The docs suggest entering scores manually only when you measure an indicator once a month, quarter, or year. That needs a person to do it, which the manager wants to avoid.
A historical data collection job collects scores and snapshots for existing records right away. It is run once, for example for a new indicator. It does not keep collecting every day.
Importing scores is suggested, like manual entry, for indicators measured once a month, quarter, or year. It is not the hands-off daily method.

source.excerpt: Performance analytics reveals trends over time... PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends.

questions.question: An analytics admin wants one role-specific page that shows recent data collection jobs with errors and gives quick access to bookmarked dashboards and visualizations. Which page should they open?

options.text: The Usage Insights application
The Platform Analytics overview page
The Data Visualizations library
The Platform Analytics Migration Center

explanation.correct: The Platform Analytics overview (All > Platform Analytics > Analytics Overview, formerly Analytics Center) gives a role-specific view of dashboards, data visualizations, indicators, filters, and scheduled exports. For admins it shows scorecards such as the latest data collection jobs with errors, plus a Quick access list with Bookmarked, Created by me, and Certified tabs. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/analytics-center.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Usage Insights provides dashboards about how users engage with registered web and mobile applications. It does not track data collection job errors.
The Data Visualizations library lists visualizations you own or that are shared with you. It does not show data collection job scorecards or bookmarked dashboards.
The Migration Center moves Core UI dashboards, reports, and widgets into Platform Analytics. It is not an overview page for monitoring analytics.

source.excerpt: To access data visualizations and dashboards, go to All, Platform Analytics, Analytics Center.

questions.question: A team lead wants to use Export in a Platform Analytics dashboard's More actions menu and attach the file to a meeting invite. Which two file types can that export produce? (Choose two)

options.text: PDF document
Excel spreadsheet
PowerPoint deck
CSV data file

explanation.correct: You can export a Platform Analytics experience dashboard to PDF or Microsoft PowerPoint. In the Export dialog, File type offers PDF or PowerPoint. For PowerPoint, each visualization gets its own slide. In a PDF, each visualization gets its own page. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/export-pae-dashboard-ppt.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: In the supported export formats table, dashboards support only PowerPoint and PDF. Microsoft Excel is listed only for a List data visualization exported on its own.
CSV is not a dashboard export format. In the supported formats table, CSV is available only when a List data visualization is exported on its own.

source.excerpt: Visualizations can be shown as bar charts, pie charts, et cetera, and can be run manually or automatically scheduled.

questions.question: A user on a net new Brazil instance wants to browse the data visualizations that colleagues have shared with them. Where should they go?

options.text: All > Platform Analytics > Library > Indicators
All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations
All > Platform Analytics > Library > Dashboards
All > Platform Analytics Administration > Data Collector > Jobs

explanation.correct: On net new Brazil instances, Reporting is replaced with Data Visualizations. You access data visualizations at All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations. Owners can access and share their visualizations, and users they share them with can access them too. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/analytics-center-data-visualizations.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Platform Analytics > Library > Indicators opens the list of indicators (KPIs), not data visualizations.
All > Platform Analytics > Library > Dashboards is where you select a dashboard, for example to share it. It lists dashboards, not data visualizations.
All > Platform Analytics Administration > Data Collector > Jobs lists Performance Analytics data collection jobs, for example to cancel one. It is not the visualization library.

questions.question: A user selects Add to Dashboard > Add to existing dashboard for a visualization, but a dashboard they own and can edit is missing from the Select dashboard list. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The visualization has not been certified yet
The target dashboard is a technical dashboard
The visualization uses an Indicator data source
The dashboard already contains a filter element

explanation.correct: When adding a visualization to an existing dashboard, the Select dashboard list shows only dashboards you can edit, and technical dashboards are not available. Because the user owns and can edit this dashboard, the remaining explanation is that it is a technical dashboard. Technical dashboards are built in UI Builder by users with the ui_builder_admin role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/add-dv-new-db.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Certification is an optional marker of company approval. It is not a prerequisite for adding a visualization to a dashboard.
Indicator is a base-system data source supported by many visualization types. The data source does not limit which dashboards appear in the list.
Inline dashboards are designed to hold filters alongside data visualizations, so an existing filter does not hide the dashboard from the list.

questions.question: A designer is building a bar visualization in the Visualization Designer. Which two of these settings are configured in its Header and border section? (Choose 2)

options.text: Chart title
Legend position
Show export options
Predefined conditions

explanation.correct: When you create a horizontal or vertical bar visualization, you first configure the Header and border. Its fields include Chart title (the title of the visualization) and Show export options (show or hide the visualization's export types). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/create-dv-bar-ac.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Legend position (Above, Below, Right, or Left) is a Legend setting under Presentation, where you provide display and color information.

Predefined conditions belong to the data source. When you select a table, you can filter it by custom or preconfigured conditions, and configured report sources appear in the Predefined conditions list.

questions.question: An analyst wants one chart that shows relationships between several incident fields so patterns that aren't obvious stand out. Which three visualization types do the docs group as multidimensional? (Choose 3)

options.text: Pivot table visualization
Heatmap visualization
Pareto bar visualization
Bubble chart visualization
Horizontal bar visualization

explanation.correct: Multidimensional visualizations show several variables in one chart and help you find patterns or trends that might not be obvious. The docs list pivot table, heatmap, and bubble chart visualizations in this group. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/data-visualization-type-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pareto bar visualizations are listed under bar visualizations. They help you find the most important dimension, with columns in descending order and a cumulative-percentage line.
Horizontal bar visualizations are bar visualizations. They compare scores across data dimensions, with categories on one axis and values on the other.

questions.question: A service desk manager's Platform Analytics dashboard has data caching turned on, and its table-based visualizations show counts from earlier in the day. The manager needs the latest incident counts right now. What should they do?

options.text: Refresh the dashboard manually
Run a historical data collection job
Schedule an export of the dashboard
Raise the dashboard tab cache timeout

explanation.correct: Data caching helps data visualizations load faster by reusing older responses when available. The docs note that users can always get the latest data by refreshing the dashboard manually. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/data-caching-pa.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A historical data collection job collects Performance Analytics scores and snapshots for existing records of an indicator. It does not update a cached dashboard of table data.
A scheduled export automates the export and mailing of dashboards and data visualizations. It does not refresh the cached data the manager sees.
The tab cache timeout is the number of minutes dashboard tab content stays cached before it is refreshed. Raising it keeps older content longer.

questions.question: An analyst wants to compare open incident counts across twelve assignment groups. Which visualization type does the docs guidance recommend for this kind of nominal data?

options.text: Horizontal bar visualization
Spline visualization
Gauge visualization
Indicator scorecard visualization

explanation.correct: Bar visualizations compare scores across data dimensions. The docs advise using horizontal bars for nominal or categorical data, and give incident severity or assignment group as examples. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/data-visualization-type-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Spline is a time series visualization. It shows how values change over time using a fitted curve, not a comparison across groups.
A gauge shows where a single value lies between a minimum and a maximum expected value. It shows one value, not a comparison across groups.
The Indicator scorecard visualizes and compares data between multiple Performance Analytics indicators. The docs recommend horizontal bars, not scorecards, for nominal data such as assignment group.

questions.question: An admin has just created an automated indicator for open incidents, and a manager wants its trend over the past several months right away. No scores have been collected yet. What should the admin do first?

options.text: Run a historical data collection job for it
Switch the visualization to a Table data source
Enable Follow filters on the trend visualization
Certify the trend visualization in the library

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics shows trends from indicator scores that data collection jobs gather. When you collect data for the first time, as with a new indicator, the docs say to run a historical data collection job once. That job generates scores and snapshots for existing records, so months of trend data become available right away. A scheduled data collection job then keeps collecting scores. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/c_ClctData.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Tables contain current data. To view trends over time you need an indicator, whose values are collected over time, so a table source cannot supply the history.
Follow filters only makes a visualization respond to interactive dashboard filters on the same table. It does not generate any indicator scores.
Certifying marks a visualization as company-approved for reuse. It has no effect on whether the indicator has collected scores.

questions.question: A team lead shared a Platform Analytics dashboard with the Service Desk group. Members can rearrange its content but cannot save their changes. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The group was added as a viewer, not an editor
The dashboard's visualizations were not shared separately
Members lack the admin or dashboard_admin role
The dashboard was shared with a group, not with users

explanation.correct: When you share a dashboard, you choose Add as viewer or Add as editor. Users who only have viewing rights can make changes to the dashboard's content but can't save them. Add as editor grants editing rights. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/share-db-in-ac.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data visualizations based on table data are shared automatically with the users you share a dashboard with. Visualizations do not need to be shared separately for the dashboard to be used.

Users with the admin or dashboard_admin role can share all dashboards, but these roles are not needed to save changes to a shared dashboard. Add as editor grants editing rights to the users, groups, or roles you share with.
You can share a dashboard with users, groups, or roles, and a group can be added as either a viewer or an editor.

questions.question: A manager wants the Incidents Overview dashboard emailed to the service desk group as a PDF every Monday morning, without anyone sending it by hand. What should the analyst set up?

options.text: A scheduled export from More actions
A one-time export with Send via email
A share of the dashboard with the group
A data caching setting on the dashboard

explanation.correct: Scheduled exports automate the export and mailing of dashboards and data visualizations. From the item's More actions menu, select Schedule. Then choose the file type, set how often the email is sent under Reoccurrence, and add users and groups as recipients. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/schedule-export-dboards-data-viz.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Export with the Send via email delivery method sends the file once, when you select Export. It does not repeat each week.
Sharing gives users, groups, or roles rights to view or edit the dashboard. It does not email them an exported file.
Data caching reuses older responses so visualizations load faster. It does not send any email.

questions.question: An analyst wants dashboard viewers who select a segment of a pie visualization of incidents to open a list of the records behind that segment. Which chart interaction action should they configure?

options.text: Go to data view action
Go to URL action
Apply as filter action
Drill down to chart action

explanation.correct: In a visualization's Chart interaction section, you set what happens when a viewer selects a segment. Go to data view opens a view of the data that fits the data type, such as a list view for table data. It is the default interaction for all supported data sources. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/dv-chart-interactions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Go to URL opens a URL you specify, on the instance or outside it. It does not open the records behind the selected segment.
Apply as filter filters all applicable data visualizations on the dashboard by the value of the selected segment. It does not open a list of records.
Drill down to chart opens a different data visualization filtered by the selected data. It does not open a record list.
